issues.description: setuptools<82 pinned in core runtime install_requires, not just CI
issues.detail: The CI scripts pin setuptools<82 to work around an mmcv build issue — that's fine, it's scoped to CI. But core/setup.py adds 'setuptools<82' to the extras/install_requires block, which leaks a CI workaround into every downstream install of autogluon.core. setuptools is a build-time tool, not a runtime dependency — pinning it in package metadata constrains every user's environment for a problem they don't have. The right data shape: CI scripts own CI pins; package metadata owns runtime needs. Don't conflate them.

issues.description: Three near-identical setuptools<82 pins with no single source of truth
issues.detail: The same pin now lives in env_setup.sh (build_pkg), setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py. When mmcv 3325 is fixed, someone has to remember all three sites. A single shared variable or a single FIXME-tracked location would make the cleanup obvious. Small thing, but the data (the version cap) wants one home, not three.

issues.description: mmcv installed with --no-build-isolation — fragile and underexplained
issues.detail: Switching to --no-build-isolation means mmcv's build now reads from the ambient environment's setuptools/torch/etc., which is why the setuptools<82 pin has to be installed in the same step beforehand. That's a real coupling and worth a one-line comment so the next person doesn't 'clean up' the pip install setuptools<82 line and break the build silently. The FIXME points at the upstream issue but doesn't explain the local ordering constraint.

issues.description: mmdet bumped 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 with no note
issues.detail: The diff also moves mmdet from 3.2.0 to 3.3.0. That may be necessary to match mmengine 0.10.7 / mmcv 2.1.0, but it's a behavior change folded into a CI-fix PR with no mention in the description. A one-line note ('mmdet 3.3.0 is the version compatible with mmengine 0.10.7') would make the intent obvious without forcing a reviewer to cross-reference release notes.

review.summary: The CI fix itself is small and composable — replace a git-SHA mmengine install with a pinned PyPI wheel, cap setuptools to dodge the upstream mmcv regression, and the algorithm (the install script) becomes obvious. Good shape. The one place the data structure is wrong is core/setup.py: a CI build-tool workaround does not belong in a published package's runtime dependency list, and shipping it there exports the workaround to every downstream user. Secondary nits: the same setuptools<82 cap is duplicated in three places with no single source of truth, --no-build-isolation introduces an ordering constraint that deserves a comment, and the mmdet 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 bump is unexplained. Strip the setuptools pin out of core/setup.py, leave the CI scripts alone, and this is a clean fix.
